title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a fragmentary page from Grothendieck's c.1965–71 notes on algebraic cycles and the standard, Hodge and Tate conjectures. Its subject is 'structures d'effectivité' (effectivity structures), and it seems to continue a numbered discussion: it refers back to item 3° and to objects i, i_1, j_1, ε, P(i), Γ', π_1, I(G) and Eff(G).

The neighbouring pages are not Grothendieck's. They are typed pages (III.6, III.7) from someone's work on sheaves of locally separable (Azumaya-type) algebras and commutants, apparently misfiled. So they give no context for this page.

Most plausible modern reading:
- There is a reductive group G (a motivic or Tannakian Galois group, or a monodromy/Mumford–Tate type group). Over a base it varies as a sheaf with monodromy π_1.
- Γ is a real vector space of invariants, for instance cycle classes or symmetric forms; Γ' is its dual.
- For an involution-type datum i (a Weil operator or Cartan involution, i.e. a candidate polarization), P(i) is the positivity cone determined by i. Concretely, it is the set of classes x on which the form ⟨x, i x⟩ is positive.
- ε is a central sign element (like the weight element w(−1)). It defines a half-space, and the 'cone of ε' is the largest admissible cone.

The first paragraph states an equivalence. Suppose an effectivity structure is defined as the intersection of the P(i) over a sheaf (family) of such i. Then giving it is the same as giving a cone C in Γ' with these properties:
- C is invariant under π_1.
- C is 'strictly' contained in the cone defined by ε.
- C contains the cone of i.
- C satisfies a saturation condition with respect to the polarizations given by i. Grothendieck asks whether this condition is automatic.
This is a duality between families of positivity data (polar cones) and convex cones.

The second paragraph takes the most natural case: M^+ (the effective part) is P(i_1), with i_1 as in 3°. The cone involved is the invariant cone generated by all the conjugates j_1 of i_1, and it lies in the half-space defined by ε, the bracket recording the normalisation ε i_1 = id. This gives a map I(G) → Eff(G), from (conjugacy classes of) polarization-type involutions to effectivity structures.

The exclamatory marginal note says this means 'ε is interior to the polar cone'. Read as an ampleness-type criterion: just as an ample class lies in the interior of the dual of the effective cone (Kleiman), the sign/weight element must lie in the interior of the polar of the effectivity cone.

The problem served is to axiomatize positivity and effectivity for motives and Tannakian categories. The goal is that the standard conjecture of Hodge type (positivity) and the notion of effective motive can be formulated purely in terms of the motivic Galois group plus cone data.
errors: The page is too fragmentary to verify. The 'saturation' condition is left as an open question ('condition automatiquement satisfaite ?').

'strictement' is in quotation marks; the strictness needed (interior versus closed cone) is not specified. The marginal remark suggests the right formulation is that ε lies in the interior of the polar cone.

ideas.what: Effectivity structure on a (motivic/Tannakian) object defined as the intersection of positivity cones P(i) over a family of polarization-type involutions; equivalence with π_1-invariant convex cones in a dual space Γ' contained in the ε-cone and saturated
ideas.modern_name: positivity/effectivity cones in Tannakian categories; polarizations of Tannakian categories (Weil forms, Cartan involutions)
ideas.where_published: Polarizations appear in Saavedra's thesis written under Grothendieck; I do not know of a published Grothendieck text on 'structures d'effectivité' (unsure)

ideas.what: Map I(G) → Eff(G) from polarization-type involutions (normalised by ε i_1 = id) to effectivity structures, via the invariant cone generated by the conjugates of i_1
ideas.modern_name: cone generated by a Cartan involution orbit; compact real forms ↔ polarizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (compact forms ↔ polarizations, Hodge-theoretic setting); Saavedra

ideas.what: Criterion that ε is interior to the polar cone (an ampleness-type condition)
ideas.modern_name: Kleiman-type duality between ample and effective cones

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a classification of 'effectivity structures' on motives / G-representations by convex cones dual to families of polarizations. He also defines a map I(G) → Eff(G), and asks whether the saturation condition is automatic. Saavedra and Deligne–Milne develop polarizations of Tannakian categories but, to my knowledge, not a parallel theory of effectivity cones (Eff(G)) dual to them.
missed.quote: la donnée d'une telle structure équivaut à celle d'un "cône" dans Γ', invariant par π_1, contenu "strictement" dans celui défini par ε ... On trouve ainsi une application I(G) → Eff(G)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Effective motives, and characterizing effectivity Tannakian-theoretically (e.g. via positivity), remain open problems related to the standard conjectures. A cone-theoretic duality between polarizations and effectivity could inform current work on positivity in motivic Galois groups (e.g. Ancona-style approaches to the standard conjecture of Hodge type).

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an unpublished notion, 'structures d'effectivité' parametrized by convex cones dual to polarizations, with a map I(G) → Eff(G). It is suggestive and does not appear in the polarization literature as such. But it is fragmentary, and its symbols are hard to pin down without the preceding pages.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring 'pages' (III.6, III.7, on locally separable sheaves of algebras) are a typed document by another author, misfiled in this cote. They are not context for this page.
'aux précisions par i' is more likely 'aux polarisations par i' or similar; the handwriting is ambiguous.
The bracketed line is probably 'où j_1 ... i_1 ... j, ε i_1 = id' (conjugates j_1 = j i_1 j^{-1}?), not 'i.e.'.
'{+NB.+}' over the crossed-out words may read 'TNB' or 'cf. NB'; uncertain.
The crossed-out first line 'À tout "cône" A(4)' is illegible; possibly 'À tout "cône" associé'.
